en: Petavatthu, Mahāvagga, 10. Gaṇapetavatthu The Story of the Group of Petas Once upon a time, there were five hundred merchants who set out from Sāvatthī on a trading journey. On their way, they encountered a great bandit chief named Aḷavaka. The bandits seized all their goods and took them away. Then those merchants, with their hands bound behind their backs, were led along the highway by the bandits. As they went, they saw a certain peta standing at the crossroads. He was naked, his body covered in sores, emaciated, and his limbs were like dry wood. His hair and beard were matted and discolored, and he was constantly crying out in distress. Seeing him, the merchants asked: "Who are you, sir? Why do you stand here naked, with sores covering your body, emaciated, with limbs like dry wood, your hair and beard matted and discolored, crying out in distress? The peta replied: "Sirs, I am a peta. They asked: "What evil deed did you commit, sir, that you have been reborn as a peta? He said: "Sirs, in the past, when people were giving alms-food to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, I would go there and say: 'Give me some too! But the donors would not give it to me. Because of that, I have been reborn as a peta. Then the merchants, having heard this, felt compassion for him and said: "Sir, we shall give alms-food to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha and dedicate the merit to you. When they had spoken thus, the peta vanished right there. The merchants then went to Sāvatthī and gave alms-food to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha. Having dedicated the merit to the peta, they returned to their own homes. At that time, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: "Bhikkhus, these five hundred merchants have performed a deed that will lead to their long-term welfare and happiness. For they have given alms-food to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha and dedicated the merit to a peta. By the power of that deed, they will enjoy heavenly bliss for many years, for many hundreds of years, for many thousands of years, and for many hundreds of thousands of years. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then those bhikkhus, having heard the Blessed One’s words, were filled with wonder and amazement. They approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported everything they had seen and heard regarding the peta. The Blessed One said: "Bhikkhus, it is not surprising that those who have done such a deed should experience the result in this very life. But even more wonderful is the fact that they have attained such a state of mind through their faith. This is the story of the Group of Petas.
“Naked, of ugly appearance,
emaciated, with veins showing all over;
a hunchback, a mere skeleton— ”
“Who are you here, O worthy ones?
“We are hungry ghosts, O venerable sir,
miserable beings belonging to the world of Yama.”
“Having committed evil deeds,
they have gone from here to the world of the departed.
“What indeed [did they do] by way of body or speech?”
An evil deed was committed with the mind;
by the ripening of what karma have you gone from here to the world of petas?
“At open fords, we searched for even a half-penny,
while things worthy of being given were still available.”
We left our own island for the sky;
thirsty, we approached the river,
but it turned out empty.
In the heat we resort to shade,
and the sunlight shifts;
and the wind has the color of fire for us.
Burning, it blows upon us;
we deserve this, O Venerable One,
and other evils even worse than that.
Even though we travel for leagues,
hungry and greedy for food,
we turn back without having obtained any.
Alas for our meager merit!
Hungry, fainting, and staggering,
we have been cast down upon the ground.
We were turned face upwards and cast down; they fell right there, face downwards.
Struck against the ground,
our chests and heads were bruised—
alas for our meager merit!
We deserve this, O Venerable One,
and even more than that, some evil deed,
while there are things worthy of being given.
They have indeed left their own celestial realm behind.
Having departed from here and obtained a human birth, they will surely...
"Generous and perfected in virtue,
we shall perform much that is wholesome.
The tenth story of the *Gaṇa-peta*.
